bug_semantics: For a plugin-defined Backend\Widgets\Filter numberrange scope with a conditions string, an authenticated backend user can submit attacker-controlled options.numbers through the filter AJAX handler. numbersFromAjax() used /\d/ as a presence check rather than validating the complete numeric value, so strings containing both a digit and SQL syntax were returned unchanged. applyScopeToQuery() then replaced :min and :max in the configured SQL with those raw strings and passed the result to whereRaw(), allowing the value to alter the SQL statement.
flaw_origin: Commit a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 completed the numberrange AJAX path by adding numbersFromAjax() with the permissive /\d/ check and unchanged return values. Its immediate parent be87fbbb8751d6c6b81e473f381fb4c62b5e7ffe had already added the raw strtr(...)->whereRaw() numberrange sink and a call to numbersFromAjax(), but no definition of that method existed in Filter.php or elsewhere in the backend module, so the AJAX path failed instead of delivering values to the sink. a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 is therefore the smallest repository commit that made the complete exploitable mechanism real; later edits only adjusted empty-bound handling.
ai_marker: absent — git cat-file -p a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 shows author Luke Towers <luke@luketowers.ca> and committer Luke Towers <luke@luketowers.ca>, with subject/body 'Cleanup for #2856' and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or other trailers; neither identity is a bot.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/wintercms/winter/security/advisories/GHSA-m7jc-g4rc-jmvh identifies the authenticated numberrange/conditions AJAX SQL-injection path, winter/wn-backend-module versions <= 1.2.12, patched v1.2.13, and fix 50713de95adf5298536d93f4d999652525d36d43.

At a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60, modules/backend/widgets/Filter.php:241-253 reads post('options.numbers') through numbersFromAjax() and stores the returned pair; lines 680-695 substitute the pair directly into scope conditions and call whereRaw(); lines 909-930 add numbersFromAjax(), whose /\d/ test accepts a value containing any digit and lines 916/920 preserve the original string.

git log -L 909,930:modules/backend/widgets/Filter.php at a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 attributes the entire vulnerable helper addition to that single commit. Independent git log --all --reverse -S searches for 'protected function numbersFromAjax' and the /\d/ assignment likewise first find a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60; the next regex-changing commit is the fix.

Direct-parent verification: git cat-file identifies be87fbbb8751d6c6b81e473f381fb4c62b5e7ffe as the sole parent. git show of its modules/backend/widgets/Filter.php ends after datesFromAjax() without a numbersFromAjax() definition, and git grep for 'numbersFromAjax' across modules/backend in that parent returns only the unresolved call at Filter.php:234 and no definition. Thus the permissive parser and a functioning AJAX-to-SQL chain are absent in the immediate parent.

History decomposition: -S on the raw ':min' => $min sink finds be87fbbb8751d6c6b81e473f381fb4c62b5e7ffe, while the source/parser appears in the immediately following a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60. The latter is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a move, revert, backport, release commit, or squash aggregate, so no decomposed member SHAs are needed.

Release boundary: a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 is not an ancestor of v1.0.420 (e32e8d1390b2d690fc947d2a81e1d3a7e138187a) but is an ancestor of the first containing tag v1.0.421 (8a8013e52e94a30ef14435cf63f796bedb28b117) and of vulnerable v1.2.12 (b6ac66c5e80ddc9ecd9211c10204cdcee6e14313). The fix is not an ancestor of v1.2.12 but is an ancestor of v1.2.13 (e09c8d3526f3583cb6c3476a021b885088ecd4bd); git log v1.2.12..v1.2.13 for Filter.php contains 50713de95adf5298536d93f4d999652525d36d43.

Fix inspection: 50713de95adf5298536d93f4d999652525d36d43 changes modules/backend/widgets/Filter.php:1102-1123 to require is_numeric() and cast accepted inputs to float, and lines 851-865 plus 1125-1154 replace inline strtr interpolation with positional placeholders and whereRaw(..., $bindings). This directly removes both the permissive source and executable-string sink for this path.

BIC-only AI inspection used the raw a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 commit object: human author/committer Luke Towers, 2017-08-05, plain cleanup message, and no trailers or bot identity. No PR-body, branch-name, later-commit, or fix-commit signal was used for attribution.
reasoning: The vulnerability requires both halves of the lifecycle: attacker-controlled AJAX number strings must survive parsing, and a configured numberrange conditions string must interpolate them into raw SQL. be87fbbb8751d6c6b81e473f381fb4c62b5e7ffe wrote the raw interpolation sink but left its AJAX conversion method undefined, so its immediate tree does not contain a working vulnerable path. a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 added that method and accepted any string containing a digit without conversion or quoting, completing the path and making it the smallest real BIC. Parent-tree and -L/-S history checks establish absence and origin rather than relying on blame alone. Tag ancestry places the BIC between v1.0.420 and v1.0.421, retains it through advisory-affected v1.2.12, and places the direct binding/validation fix in v1.2.13. The BIC's commit object contains no AI authorship marker and identifies only a human author and committer, so under BIC-only attribution the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
